Today is 2026-04-29. I need current (last 3 months: Jan 29 - Apr 29 2026) projects and discussions about a very specific architecture pattern.

**The pattern**: A search/retrieval system where:
- All data lives in object storage (S3/R2/GCS or local filesystem dir) as content-addressed chunks
- Index lives mostly in object storage too (split files, periodically flushed)
- Hot copy of index lives in memory of a single process (think MCP server, edge worker, serverless function)
- On cold start: download index file from bucket, load into memory, replay any chunks newer than index timestamp
- Supports: BM25 / full-text search, vector kNN, structured filters, recursive parent traversal
- Multi-tenant by namespace = bucket prefix or separate buckets
- No SQL backend at all (no Postgres, no SQLite)

This is the Loki TSDB-shipper / Quickwit split-file pattern, but for the AI session vault / agent memory / RAG use case (sessions, messages, parts, embeddings) instead of logs.

## What I want

Identify CURRENT Rust / Go / TypeScript / Bun projects (libraries, runtimes, products) that solve this exact problem or a close adjacent problem. Active in 2026.

Prioritize:
1. **Libraries** I could embed in a TS/Bun process (preferred)
2. **Self-hostable engines** that run as a sidecar with object storage as primary
3. **Patterns / blog posts / discussions** showing how people are solving this in 2026

Specific candidates to verify activity for (just check 2025-2026 commit activity, latest release, recent issues):
- Orama (oramasearch/orama) - TS-native, claimed FTS+vectors+filters in one
- Quickwit - Rust, log-style index on S3
- Tantivy / tantivy-binding - Rust full-text
- usearch - vector lib
- LanceDB - Rust embedded vector DB on object storage
- DuckDB + extensions - has FTS, has vector, has S3 support
- Turbopuffer - serverless vector DB
- ChromaDB - latest activity
- Vectroid, Marqo, Vespa - any object-storage native options
- Sled, Fjall - embedded KV (Rust)
- pglite, electric-sql, turso - edge SQLite alternatives (note: user wants to drop SQL, so these are negative examples but worth flagging)

Also check anything new launched in 2026 specifically. People are building "agent memory" / "session storage" infra fast right now.

## Search plan

Use paymentservice_a tools (NOT WebSearch/WebFetch):
- `mcp__paymentservice_a__paymentservice_a_github_search` - kind=repos with `created:>2025-10-29` or similar to find new ones
- `mcp__paymentservice_a__paymentservice_a_github_search` - kind=conversations to find discussions
- `mcp__paymentservice_a__paymentservice_a_github_get` - kind=commits/releases to verify activity dates
- `mcp__paymentservice_a__paymentservice_a_reddit_search` - subreddit:rust, subreddit:golang, subreddit:LocalLLaMA, subreddit:LangChain, subreddit:rag etc
- `mcp__paymentservice_a__paymentservice_a_reddit_subreddit` - hot/top in r/rust, r/MachineLearning
- `mcp__paymentservice_a__paymentservice_a_web_search` with start_published_date filter for 2026
- HackerNews via `paymentservice_a_web_search` or `paymentservice_a_web_crawl` on hn.algolia.com

Use start_published_date="2026-01-29" on web_search and start_date="2026-01-29" on github/reddit searches to enforce the 3-month window.

## Output format

Tight, scannable. Group by language. For each project:
- One-line summary of what it does
- Why it matches (or doesn't quite match) the pattern
- Activity signal: latest release date, latest commit, GitHub stars, Reddit/HN buzz
- Linkable URL

End with a recommendation block: top 3 picks for "embed in TS/Bun MCP process, store everything in object storage".

Under 800 words. Be honest if there's no perfect match - "X is closest but it's a sidecar daemon, not embeddable" is a useful answer. Cite real evidence with URLs/dates, no speculation, no making up version numbers or stars.

# litesearch

A fully-local semantic search CLI. Ingest documents, embed them locally, and run vector search — no external services required.

## How it works

`litesearch ingest` runs a document through a four-stage pipeline:

1. **Parse**: extracts plain text from the file using [LiteParse](https://github.com/run-llama/liteparse)
2. **Chunk**: splits the text into overlapping segments using [Chonkie](https://github.com/chonkie-ai/chonkie) (default: 512 characters)
3. **Embed**: generates 768-dimensional embeddings locally using [`nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`](https://huggingface.co/nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5) via `@huggingface/transformers`
4. **Store**: upserts vectors and payloads into a local [Qdrant Edge](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant-edge) shard persisted at `.litesearch.qdrant/`

`litesearch retrieve` embeds the query with the same model and performs a cosine similarity search against the local shard.

The vector store is backed by `qdrant-edge-utils`, a Rust native addon (napi-rs) that wraps `qdrant-edge` for on-disk mmap-backed storage.

## Requirements

- [Bun](https://bun.sh)
- Rust toolchain (only needed if rebuilding `qdrant-edge-utils` from source)

## Installation

```sh
bun install
```

## Usage

### Ingest a document

```sh
bun run ingest <file> [options]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config ` | Path to a LiteParse config file |
| `-s, --chunk-size ` | Chunk size in characters (default: 512) |

### Search

```sh
bun run retrieve <query> [options]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-f, --files ` | Restrict search to specific ingested document paths |
| `-l, --limit ` | Maximum number of results (default: 10) |
| `-t, --score-threshold ` | Minimum cosine similarity score |

### Example

```sh
bun run ingest ./data/report.pdf
bun run retrieve "quarterly revenue breakdown" --limit 5
```

Output:

```
[0.8723] ./data/report.pdf
Revenue for Q3 reached $4.2M, up 18% from the prior quarter...

[0.8341] ./data/report.pdf
The board approved a revised forecast of $17M for the full fiscal year...
```

## TUI

You can also use the terminal interface to access the ingestion and retrieval functionalities interactively:

```bash
bun run tui
```

You can then follow the prompts from terminal, as in this image:

![TUI example](./assets/tui.png)

Hey! It's a great question. Co-founder of Vectroid here.

Today, the differences are going to be performance, price, accuracy, flexibility, and some intangible UI elegance.

Performance: We actually INITIALLY built Vectroid for the use-case of billions of vectors and near single digit millisecond latency. During the process of building and talking to users, we found that there are just not that many use-cases (yet!) that are at that scale and require that latency. We still believe the market will get there, but it's not there today. So we re-focused on building a general purpose vector search platform, but we stayed close to our high performance roots, and we're seeing better query performance than the other serverless, object storage backed vector DBs. We think we can get way faster too.

Price: We optimized the heck out of this thing with object storage, pre-emptible virtual machines, etc. We've driven our cost down, and we're passing this to the user, starting with a free tier of 100GB. Actual pricing beyond that coming soon.

Accuracy: With our initial testing, we see recall greater or equal to competitors out there, all while being faster.

Flexibility: We are going to have a self managed version for users who want to run on their own infra, but admittedly, we don't have that today. Still working on it.

Other Product Elegance: My co-founder, Talip, made Hazelcast, and I've always been impressed by how easy it is to use and how the end to end experience is so elegant. As we continue to develop Vectroid, that same level of polish and focus on the UX will be there. As an example, one neat thing we rolled out is direct import of data from Hugging Face. We have lots of other cool ideas.

## ensureOllamaReady() called unconditionally in codebase_search, breaks OpenAI/Google embedding providers

- Author: [@pineapplestrikesback](https://github.com/pineapplestrikesback)
- Association: CONTRIBUTOR
- State: closed (completed)
- Created: 2026-03-16T15:19:30Z
- Updated: 2026-03-17T17:46:53Z
- Closed: 2026-03-17T17:46:53Z
- Closed by: [@giancarloerra](https://github.com/giancarloerra)

## Description

The `codebase_search` handler in `src/tools/query-tools.ts` calls `ensureOllamaReady()` on every search request regardless of the configured `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER`. This blocks search execution for users of OpenAI or Google embeddings.

## Bug Details

In `query-tools.ts` (line 41 in the compiled output), the search handler runs:

```js
case "codebase_search": {
    await ensureQdrantReady();
    await ensureOllamaReady();  // <-- unconditional
```

When `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=openai` or `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=google`, this call fails depending on `OLLAMA_MODE`:

| `OLLAMA_MODE` | Failure |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` (default) | Creates a Docker container for Ollama, attempts to pull the configured embedding model (e.g. `text-embedding-3-large`) from Ollama's registry, fails because it is not an Ollama model |
| `docker` | Same as above |
| `external` | Tries to reach `localhost:11434`, fails with "Ollama is not reachable" |

The search never executes despite `generateQueryEmbedding()` correctly routing through `getEmbeddingProvider()`, which respects the `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER` setting.

## Expected Behavior

`ensureOllamaReady()` should only be called when `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER === "ollama"`.

## Suggested Fix

```js
case "codebase_search": {
    await ensureQdrantReady();
    if (getEmbeddingConfig().embeddingProvider === "ollama") {
        await ensureOllamaReady();
    }
```

## Workaround

Manually commenting out the `await ensureOllamaReady();` line in `dist/tools/query-tools.js` in the npx cache allows search to work correctly with non-Ollama providers.

## Environment

- **socraticode**: v1.1.2 (also reproduced on v1.0.1)
- **OS**: macOS, Docker Desktop
- **Config**: `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=openai`, `EMBEDDING_MODEL=text-embedding-3-large`

## Additional Context

The `codebase_health` tool correctly identifies OpenAI as the active embedding provider and reports it as healthy. Only the `codebase_search` code path has this unconditional Ollama dependency. Other tools that use embeddings (e.g. indexing) may have the same issue but were not tested.

{"data":"# Uni: Embedded Graph & Vector Database

[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0)
[![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.75+-orange.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org)
[![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org)

**Uni** is an embedded database that combines a property graph (OpenCypher), vector search, and columnar storage (Lance) into a single engine. Designed for applications requiring local, fast, multimodal data access with object storage (S3/GCS/local) durability.

Part of [The Rustic Initiative](https://www.rustic.ai) by [Dragonscale Industries Inc.](https://www.dragonscale.ai)

## Key Features

- **Embedded & Serverless:** Runs as a library within your application — no server process.
- **Property Graph:** OpenCypher queries with MATCH, CREATE, WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT, and aggregations.
- **Vector Search:** K-NN similarity search (L2, cosine) with pre-filter and threshold support.
- **Columnar Storage:** Lance-backed persistence on local disk or object storage (S3/GCS).
- **Graph Algorithms:** PageRank, Louvain, shortest path, and more via the built-in algorithm library.
- **Rust & Python:** Native Rust crate and Python bindings (PyO3).

## Getting Started

### Rust

Add to your `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[dependencies]
uni-db = "0.1.3"
```

### Python

```bash
pip install uni-db
```

```python
import uni_db

# Open or create a database
db = uni_db.Database("./my_graph")

# Define schema
db.create_label("Person")
db.add_property("Person", "name", "string", False)
db.add_property("Person", "age", "int64", True)
db.create_scalar_index("Person", "name", "btree")

# Write data
db.execute("CREATE (p:Person {name: 'Alice', age: 30})")
db.execute("CREATE (p:Person {name: 'Bob', age: 25})")
db.flush()

# Query
results = db.query(
    "MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.age > $min RETURN p.name",
    {"min": 28},
)
print(results)  # [{'p.name': 'Alice'}]
```

## Vector Search

```python
# Create schema with a vector property
db.create_label("Document")
db.add_property("Document", "text", "string", False)
db.add_property("Document", "embedding", "vector[128]", True)
db.create_vector_index("Document", "embedding", "cosine")

# Insert data
db.execute("CREATE (d:Document {text: 'hello world', embedding: [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]})")
db.flush()

# K-NN search
results = db.query("""
    CALL uni.vector.query('Document', 'embedding', $vec, 10)
    YIELD vid, distance
    RETURN vid, distance
    ORDER BY distance
""", {"vec": my_embedding})

# K-NN with pre-filter
results = db.query("""
    CALL uni.vector.query('Document', 'embedding', $vec, 10, 'category = "tech"')
    YIELD vid, distance
    RETURN vid, distance
""", {"vec": my_embedding})
```

## Async API

```python
import uni_db

db = await uni_db.AsyncDatabase.open("./my_graph")

await db.execute("CREATE (p:Person {name: 'Alice', age: 30})")
results = await db.query("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name")
```

## Python OGM (uni-pydantic)

```bash
pip install uni-pydantic
```

```python
from uni_pydantic import UniNode, UniSession, Field, Relationship, Vector

class Person(UniNode):
    name: str
    age: int | None = None
    email: str = Field(unique=True, index="btree")
    embedding: Vector[128] = Field(metric="cosine")
    friends: list["Person"] = Relationship("FRIEND_OF", direction="both")

session = UniSession(db)
session.register(Person)
session.sync_schema()

alice = Person(name="Alice", email="alice@example.com")
session.add(alice)
session.commit()

adults = session.query(Person).filter(Person.age >= 18).order_by(Person.name).all()
```

# Object-storage-native search/retrieval - state of the field, Jan-Apr 2026

## TypeScript / Bun (embeddable in MCP process)

**[Orama](https://github.com/oramasearch/orama)** - 10.3K stars, last release v3.1.18 on 2025-12-19, last push 2026-02-13. TS, in-2KB FTS+vector+hybrid, runs in browser/edge/server. Has `@orama/plugin-data-persistence` (binary file save/restore - exactly the pattern you want; example in [andrea9293/mcp-documentation-server commit](https://github.com/andrea9293/mcp-documentation-server/commit/09a66ad0ed8af9afad4714d440546c9bcb83ab5e), Feb 2026). NO native S3 connector - you'd write the upload/download yourself, but it's two functions. Closest match for your spec.

**[oramasearch/oramacore](https://github.com/oramasearch/oramacore)** - companion Rust runtime, v1.2.37 on 2026-03-16. Their new [oramacore_fields](https://github.com/oramasearch/oramacore_fields) (Feb 2026, v0.1.2) is a Rust on-disk field-index library with the live-layer + memmap compacted layer + periodic compaction split - directly Loki-shipper-ish.

**[retriv](https://github.com/harlan-zw/retriv)** - 22 stars, created 2026-02-02, latest v0.13.0 (2026-03-23), 1.7K weekly npm. Hybrid BM25+vector with RRF, drivers for SQLite/Turso/Upstash/Cloudflare/pgvector. SQL-ish backends - **negative example for your "no SQL" rule** but architecturally very clean, would not be hard to add an S3 driver.

**[memsearch-core](https://www.npmjs.com/package/memsearch-core)** - v1.4.1 on 2026-03-05. Markdown-first agent memory, embedded LanceDB default (object-store ready) or Milvus. Tiny (17 weekly downloads) but the shape matches.

**[smysle/agent-memory](https://github.com/smysle/agent-memory)** - 10 stars, v5.1.0 on 2026-03-20. SQLite-first BM25+optional vectors, MCP/HTTP/CLI. SQLite is a hard "no" for you, but the lifecycle model (write-guard, reflect, surface) is the best-articulated agent-memory contract I found.

**[rohitg00/agentmemory](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory)** - 2056 stars, v0.9.3 on 2026-04-24, very active. BM25+vector+graph RRF. SQLite-backed. Proves there's a hot market for the use case but does not match the object-storage requirement.

## Rust (sidecar / engine)

**[Quickwit](https://github.com/quickwit-oss/quickwit)** - 11.1K stars. Last GA tag is still v0.8.2 (June 2024); but Lambda builds shipping monthly: [lambda-11587c00 on 2026-04-21](https://github.com/quickwit-oss/quickwit/releases). Append-only, immutable - works for chat history, not for editable agent memory. Sidecar, not embeddable.

**[Tantivy](https://github.com/quickwit-oss/tantivy)** - 15.1K stars, push 2026-04-28. Pure Rust full-text lib, no S3 layer (Quickwit is the cloud wrapper around it).

**[LanceDB](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb)** - 10.1K stars, releasing every few days; latest v0.28.0-beta.10 on 2026-04-28. Embedded retrieval lib, Lance columnar format on local fs or S3/GCS. Has Node bindings. Very close to your requirements - vector + (now reduced) FTS, parent traversal via SQL-like filters, multi-tenant via tables. Note: 2026-04-28 release "removes legacy tantivy FTS support" - they're refactoring full-text, watch for churn.

**[Chroma](https://github.com/chroma-core/chroma)** - 27.7K stars, v1.5.8 on 2026-04-16, daily commits. Rewritten in Rust, uses S3 as primary store (their `wal3` log on S3 with put-stream uploads, fault injection, sharding all landed in v1.5.7-1.5.8). Sidecar service, not embeddable in TS.

**[SlateDB](https://github.com/slatedb/slatedb)** - 2.9K stars, push 2026-04-29. "Cloud native embedded storage engine built on object storage." LSM tree on S3 with CAS-based coordination. KV only, not search - but it's the foundation layer multiple projects are building search on top of. Worth tracking.

**[Fjall](https://github.com/fjall-rs/fjall)** - 2K stars, latest 3.1.4 on 2026-04-14. Local LSM only, no S3. Negative example - if you wanted Sled-style local KV you'd pick Fjall (Sled last meaningful commits Apr 2026 but project still flagged "beta").

**[rustic-ai/uni-db](https://github.com/rustic-ai/uni-db)** - **NEW Jan 2026, 31 stars.** Embedded Rust+Python that combines OpenCypher graph + vector kNN + Lance columnar, "backed by object storage (S3/GCS) durability." Tiny user base but on paper this is the closest single library to your spec for graph+vector+filters with S3 as the substrate. No FTS yet though.

**[SpillwaveSolutions/agent-memory](https://github.com/SpillwaveSolutions/agent-memory)** - 10 stars, created 2026-01-29, v2.7.0 on 2026-03-22. Rust gRPC daemon, RocksDB local. Hierarchical TOC (Year/Month/Week/Day) for agent conversation memory. Local only - useful as a design reference for time-hierarchical agent memory.

**[agentralabs/agentic-memory](https://github.com/agentralabs/agentic-memory)** - 10 stars, Feb 2026. Single-file `.amem` binary with BM25+graph+temporal indexes, content-addressed BLAKE3 chains, 4-tier hot/warm/cold/frozen storage. Single-file portability - close to your "all in object storage" feel without actually being on S3 yet.

## Patterns and discussions (the gold)

**[Turbopuffer architecture trace](https://medium.com/@ajay-edupuganti/how-turbopuffer-serves-2-5-trillion-vectors-on-s3-7d7ab7f9a7fa)** (Apr 12, 2026) - 15-min deep dive on how the production system works: centroid (SPFresh) index over S3, three-tier DRAM/NVMe/S3 cache, **single JSON file on S3 + S3 CAS as the entire coordination layer**, no Raft/Paxos/Kafka. They just wrote ["A distributed queue in a single JSON file on object storage"](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47099401) (HN, this week). This is the exact pattern you described and the canonical reference.

**[Nikhil Benesch ScyllaDB tech talk](https://scylladb.com/tech-talk/turbopuffer-a-trillions-scale-search-engine-on-object-storage)** (March 2026) and slides on [SlideShare](https://slideshare.net/slideshow/turbopuffer-a-trillions-scale-search-engine-on-object-storage-by-nikhil-benesch/286382372) - blueprint of their `./tpuf` binary architecture.

**[Ask HN: Is there an open source "companyone"?](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46318635)** - asked ~4 months ago, only 2 points, basically zero answers. Confirmed gap in OSS.

**[Vectroid HN exchange](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=45224854)** - founder explains: Java + modified Lucene + custom GCS FileSystem. Closed, k8s-managed.

**[Cognee on Tigris guide](https://tigrisdata.com/docs/agents/agent-cognee)** (March 2026) - best operational walkthrough of running a real "agent memory on S3" stack: Cognee ([cognee-ai/cognee](https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee)) using LanceDB+Kuzu+SQLite all rooted at `s3://...` URIs via `STORAGE_BACKEND=s3`. Closest publicly-documented ready-to-deploy reference.

## Top 3 picks for "embed in TS/Bun MCP, everything in object storage"

1. **Orama + a thin S3 sync layer**. Persistence plugin gives you full-bytes save/restore today; you wrap save with `PutObject` and load with `GetObject + If-None-Match`. Use prefixes per tenant. You inherit FTS + vector + filters in 80 KB. Active, TS-native, no SQL. Closest to spec for an embeddable solution.

2. **LanceDB Node bindings on R2/S3**. Already implements split-file index pattern on object storage with read-through cache. Vector + filters work great today; FTS is in flux as of 2026-04-28 - if you can lean on hybrid through reranking, fine, otherwise pair with Orama for BM25. Multi-tenant via tables. Real production users.

3. **Roll your own using SlateDB + Tantivy + usearch**, exposed through napi-rs (or call Tantivy from Bun via FFI). This is what Turbopuffer, Chroma, and uni-db are doing internally. Most work, max fit. Six months of effort. Only justified if (1) and (2) don't pan out at your scale.

Honest summary: **there is no drop-in OSS companyone for TS yet** - HN confirmed this in March. Orama with manual S3 sync is the pragmatic 90% answer for an MCP server today. LanceDB if you can tolerate a Rust-via-NAPI dependency and a brief FTS rebuild window.
